reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: 1 adds to one bucket in one subframe, coalesced: the bucket marked pending, flushed by a subframe-close callback
reading.floor: adaptive by listener: with no content-change listener every change is written, settled and announced at once, and the bucket is pushed once into the channel-owned array only when it is releasable (unheld); with a listener it behaves as the adaptive arm
reading.caveat: 1 adds to ONE bucket inside one subframe. No content-change listener. Held scenarios never reach the array on this arm when no listener exists, so they price the immediate path plus one listener-count check and one hold-count check per add. Unheld scenarios also pay one push per bucket and its release check at the close. The model reads releasability as holdCount 0; the shipped release policy is the default, which releases an unheld bucket only when it is empty. One operation is one member add. Both arms open the same nested subframe around each add, push the member into the bucket store, and close the frame after every outer subframe; emptying the stores there is timed on both arms alike. The bucket slot is held and has one effect, so the channel write door takes its effect path: the first write of a frame schedules the effect and the rest find it scheduled. The bodies copy OIMBucketWriter.markBucketSlotChanged, OIMChannel.writeWithoutFlushCheck and closeSubframe, and OIMSlotContentOwner.settleWrite, contentChanged and its subframe delivery, as of 2026-10-21. The release policy is the default one, which does nothing on a write, so neither arm calls it.
